Yes. 

The central turning point of the story—getting stranded by the incoming tide—is both surprising and appropriate. It is surprising because Toby is introduced as a meticulous marine biologist who studies tide communities and carries an official tide chart in a ziplock bag ("a man who protects his facts from the weather"). The reader expects him to be an expert on this exact environment. However, the turn is entirely appropriate to the themes and character development: they get stuck because they have spent the whole summer lingering to avoid saying goodbye, and as Toby later confesses, he misread the chart because he was distracted by watching the narrator and worrying about the impending end of their time together. Furthermore, their physical predicament appropriately mirrors their emotional state—forcing two people who refuse to talk about the future to be "genuinely, physically, mutually stuck" until they finally confess their feelings.
